    Plot calibration outputs across prey values

    plot_calibration_outputs.Rd

    Creates calibration plots showing the relationship between prey values and key model outputs used for seabORD calibration. The function displays adult mass loss and chick productivity across the range of prey values tested and highlights the prey range satisfying the specified calibration criteria.

    Usage

    plot_calibration_outputs(
  sbordout,
  calibration,
  masslower = 0.09,
  massupper = 0.11,
  prodlower = 0.45,
  produpper = 0.55
)

    Arguments

    sbordout

    A seabORD output object containing calibration results, including output_a0$data and output_c0$data.

    calibration

    A data frame returned by find_calibration_range() containing prey values and logical indicators of whether adult, chick and combined calibration criteria are met.

    masslower

    Lower acceptable bound for proportional adult mass loss. Defaults to 0.09.

    massupper

    Upper acceptable bound for proportional adult mass loss. Defaults to 0.11.

    prodlower

    Lower acceptable bound for chick productivity (ChicksPerNest). Defaults to 0.45.

    produpper

    Upper acceptable bound for chick productivity (ChicksPerNest). Defaults to 0.55.

    Value

    A two-panel plot (a gtable object produced by gridExtra::grid.arrange()) showing:

    • Adult mass loss as a function of prey value.

    • Chick productivity (chicks per nest) as a function of prey value.

    The light blue shaded region indicates prey values that satisfy both the adult mass-loss and chick-productivity criteria simultaneously. Grey dashed horizontal lines indicate the calibration bounds used to define acceptable ("moderate") conditions.

    Details

    Adult mass loss is calculated as: $$ (BM\_adult\_t0.mn - BM\_adult.mn) / BM\_adult\_t0.mn $$

    The calibration range is determined using find_calibration_range(). Prey values within the shaded region satisfy both the adult and chick calibration criteria and may be used as candidate prey values for subsequent scenario simulations.

    See also

    find_calibration_range() for identifying prey values that satisfy the calibration criteria.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) {
sbordout <- example_calibration_output_dd

calibration <- find_calibration_range(
  sbordout = sbordout,
  masslower = 0.09,
  massupper = 0.11,
  prodlower = 0.45,
  produpper = 0.55
)

plot_calibration_outputs(
  sbordout = sbordout,
  calibration = calibration,
  masslower = 0.09,
  massupper = 0.11,
  prodlower = 0.45,
  produpper = 0.55
)
}
